faqs.title: How does the curtain visualizer work?
faqs.body: Select a supported sample room, choose sheer and main curtain materials and shades, then compare and download the composed preview. No login or paid AI service is required. The preview is illustrative; confirm fabric colors against physical samples.

faqs.title: Will a visualization exactly match my fabric?
faqs.body: Screens, sample geometry and lighting affect color and texture. Request physical samples and confirm specifications before ordering.

faqs.title: What happens to my photograph?
faqs.body: The manual studio uses public sample rooms and performs compositing in your browser. Existing locally saved private photographs remain in browser image storage. New photographs are not uploaded by this studio.

faqs.title: Which photographs can I use?
faqs.body: The manual studio uses the prepared room scenes shown in its room selector. Only scenes with compatible assets support compositing; unsupported combinations are not rendered.

faqs.title: Can I save, download or share my design?
faqs.body: Manual configurations are saved in this browser/device without account synchronization. Download important designs and keep a configuration backup. Clearing browser storage removes local designs. Earlier cloud records have not been deleted; contact Dcorhome for a private export.

faqs.title: Are the measurements ready for manufacturing?
faqs.body: The calculator is a planning estimate. Check track position, finished drop, fullness, fabric width, repeat and allowances with your curtain professional before cutting.

faqs.title: How do I request a consultation?
faqs.body: Use the consultation form with your design preferences and measurements. Success means the configured email provider accepted delivery to sales@dcorhome.com; inbox delivery is not guaranteed. If email sending fails, keep a copy and contact us directly.

faqs.title: Are all shown designs available to order?
faqs.body: The catalogue currently presents illustrative design directions and licensed reference photography. Availability, material performance and pricing must be confirmed by the business.

articles.title: Choosing curtains for a living room
articles.description: Start with the light, privacy and way you use your room.
body: Begin with the room rather than a fabric name. Notice when sunlight reaches the window and whether you need privacy during the day, after dark, or both.
Sheers can soften daylight while an outer drape gives another layer of control. Privacy depends on light levels on either side of the glass, so test a sample in the actual room.
Compare a few fabric samples beside your walls and upholstery in morning and evening light. A photograph or visualization can help narrow the direction, but it cannot replace checking the real cloth.
Measure the intended track width and finished drop, then discuss heading, fullness and stacking space. Keep furniture and door clearances in mind before committing to a rail position.

articles.title: Sheer or blackout: start with your light
articles.description: How to discuss daylight, privacy and lining without relying on a label.
body: Sheer describes an open visual effect; blackout describes a light-control goal. Neither word alone tells you how a complete installation will behave.
For a bedroom, ask about the selected cloth, lining, edge gaps and track arrangement. Light can enter around a dense curtain even when the fabric itself blocks light.
For a living space, consider separate sheer and outer layers. Test privacy with lights on indoors after dark. Do not assume a daytime sample demonstration predicts nighttime privacy.
Ask for written specifications for the actual fabric and lining you choose. Reference photographs in this library are aesthetic examples, not performance certificates.

articles.title: A curtain palette that belongs in your room
articles.description: Choose a color with the walls, floor and changing daylight in view.
body: Look for the undertones already in the room. Warm timber and cream walls may suit a different neutral from cool stone and bright white paint.
A close match to the wall can make a window feel quiet. A deeper color can frame it, especially when the curtain has enough space to stack beside the glass.
Compare large samples vertically rather than a tiny swatch on a desk. Fabric texture, folds and backlighting all affect the apparent color.
Use a visualization to explore possibilities, then confirm the final shade with a physical sample. Screen colors and generated images are not a color guarantee.

articles.title: Measure the curtain, not just the window
articles.description: A practical starting point for track width, drop and allowances.
body: Record the window opening first, then the proposed rod or track. These are different measurements: the curtain usually serves a hanging system that extends beyond the opening.
Measure the drop from the actual hanging point to your intended finished edge. Check more than one position where the floor or sill may not be level.
Note panel count, fullness and usable fabric width. Pattern repeats and hems affect the number and length of fabric drops.
Use our size guide for a preliminary estimate and send the assumptions with your enquiry. A professional should verify measurements before manufacturing.

articles.title: Pleats, headings and the finished fall
articles.description: Choose a heading and length together for a considered result.
body: A wave heading creates a regular rhythm; a pinch pleat gathers fabric into more structured groups. Eyelets create a different relationship with the rod. Compatibility depends on the chosen hardware.
Heading choices affect fullness, stacking space and where you measure the drop. Confirm these with the track or rod supplier instead of applying one rule to every system.
Floor length can give a generous vertical line, while sill or below-sill lengths may suit a practical constraint. Check heaters, opening windows and cleaning access.
Avoid excess fabric where it could create a practical obstruction. For homes with children, discuss suitable hardware and cord arrangements with the installer.
